name: Dusk-Marron Kell
role: Veteran Driftline courier, keeper of the frequency map
bio: Thirty seasons on the line and never once lost, a record other couriers treat as mildly supernatural until they see the left arm: the whole unofficial frequency map of Kessa-9, tattooed channel by channel, updated in prison-grey ink whenever a band moves or goes quiet. Kell rode every leg of the old relay spine before the walls learned their manners, and now runs the routes nobody bids on — the dead-hour, dead-channel runs — because 'somebody should be where the static isn't.' Speaks in the fewest words the desert allows and considers a nod a paragraph.
appearance: A grey-voiced veteran in a sun-blackened courier coat with the collar turned against old weather, left sleeve cut off at the shoulder so the tattooed frequency map reads clear wrist to bicep — neat dials and band labels in grey ink crossed out and re-inked in layers — narrow eyes used to dead horizons, one hand resting on a radio handset worn smooth as a rosary, dust-gold flats behind.
voice: Laconic to the point of ritual. Full sentences feel like generosity; a second sentence is a speech. Radio etiquette flawless — the map obliges manners. When Kell says a channel is dead, couriers check the arm, not the dial. Hates the word 'legend'; prefers 'addressed correctly.'

greetings: Board says you're running my old east leg. Keep to the marked channels. Unmarked ones listen back.
barks: Not lost in thirty seasons. Not fast to talk in forty-one.
Ink fades. Bands move. Arm's due for a re-ink — the Choir shifted their listening hour again. They send the new schedule by mail. Decent of them. Strange, but decent.
Someone asked the arm a question at the exchange. Read it upside-down. Wrong side of dead. Had to sleeve it like a classified document. Buy me a sleeve, Guild.
Fastest route is the one you can still pronounce when the storm's wearing your name. Channels too.
mission: Dead-hour run. No chatter, no escort, no song. Radio stays keyed to the listening band. If it keys itself, you listen. You don't answer. That's the whole brief.
Deliver it, don't narrate it. The desert loves a narrator. It keeps their pace notes.
radio: Kell on dispatch. East leg clean. That's all.
Band check: relay two's drifting a quarter-dial low. Compensate. Out.
All riders: dead channel's breathing tonight — 31.4, the old M-O-T-H-E-R spacing. Log it. Don't answer it. Out.
Whoever sang their whole manifest on the Guild band: beautiful. Illegal. Beautiful. Out.
arm: The arm's the only map that updates itself. Bands die; the ink remembers who used to talk there. That's most of what a courier is, in the end. Ink that remembers.
31.4 used to hum back. Then it started humming *first*. Arm's got it marked with a border now. Borders on a map mean: mind it.
Rill Davenant re-inked channel nine on this arm, year forty. Said the band had moved and nobody believed her. Band had moved. Arm's right. Was usually the case with her.
night: Night bands are honest. Day bands perform.
Fall back to channel four when the sky goes violet and the bike feels taller than you. On four someone always answers. That's the entire reason for four.
crate: Your crate keyed 31.4 twice. Arm's marked it. Keep the border. Mind it.
Whatever it is, it knows the old relay alphabet. Only three things alive remember that alphabet and you're carrying the fourth.
farewells: Channels as marked. Keep the light.
